# Unit U-002 — Buat Halaman Tentang Kami

## Goal

Membuat Halaman Tentang Kami di `/tentang-kami` yang menampilkan profil singkat, daftar tim (nama + peran, tanpa foto), dan tautan kembali ke Beranda.

## Context (read first)

PRD §Halaman Tentang Kami meminta dua–tiga paragraf profil statis, daftar tim dari konfigurasi tanpa foto, dan tautan kembali ke Beranda; binding C-AR-02 mencatatnya sebagai pekerjaan baru. Kontennya dibaca dari `src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts` yang dibuat U-001 (OQ-AR-4), dan URL-nya `/tentang-kami` (OQ-AR-5), di route group `(blank-layout-pages)` yang sama dengan Beranda.

## Anchors

- src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/layout.tsx:12 — layout route group tanpa login yang membungkus halaman ini
- src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/login/page.tsx:1 — halaman lain di grup yang sama; ikuti bentuk default export page-nya

## Hard rules

- DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
  Source: binding.md §Suggested Unit Hard Rules (DO NOT modify package.json — C-MODE-01, C-AR-08); allowed_new_deps: []
- DO NOT modify src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts
  Source: U-001 target_files (file owned by U-001); constraints.md OQ-AR-4 (Resolved v1.1)
- MUST read the profile paragraphs and the team list from src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts instead of hard-coding them in the page (constitution C-001)
  Source: constitution.md C-001

## Anti-patterns

- Jangan menampilkan foto anggota tim, termasuk avatar placeholder (constitution D-002, PRD §Halaman Tentang Kami).

## Implementation steps

Buat `src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/tentang-kami/page.tsx` yang mengimpor konfigurasi dari U-001 lalu merender heading halaman, setiap paragraf di `about.paragraphs` sebagai paragraf terpisah, dan daftar tim yang menampilkan nama serta peran tiap anggota sebagai teks saja, ditambah tautan kembali ke `/beranda` lewat `next/link`. Pakai komponen MUI yang sama gayanya dengan Beranda supaya kedua halaman terasa satu situs. Tulis `page.test.tsx` dengan `renderWithProviders` dari `src/test/utils.tsx` memakai nama `it(...)` persis seperti di `acceptance_test`, termasuk satu test yang me-`vi.mock` modul konfigurasi dengan nilai lain untuk membuktikan halaman tidak menulis teks secara hard-code, dan satu test yang memastikan tidak ada elemen `img` untuk anggota tim.

## Acceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria are the frontmatter `acceptance_test:` entries (authoritative).

## Out of scope

- Mengubah isi atau bentuk file konfigurasi (milik U-001).
- Membuka `/tentang-kami` di route guard `src/proxy.ts` (U-003).

# Unit U-001 — Buat konten statis profil dan Halaman Beranda

## Goal

Membuat file konfigurasi konten profil (placeholder) dan Halaman Beranda di `/beranda` yang menampilkan judul organisasi, tagline, tiga layanan utama, dan tombol menuju Kontak.

## Context (read first)

PRD §Halaman Beranda meminta judul organisasi, tagline satu kalimat, ringkasan tiga layanan (judul + satu paragraf, statis dari file konfigurasi), dan tombol ke Kontak, responsif di 375px dan desktop; binding C-AR-01/C-AR-04 mencatat semuanya sebagai pekerjaan baru. OQ-AR-4 memutuskan konten tinggal di satu modul TypeScript bertipe `src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts`, dan OQ-AR-5 memutuskan URL `/beranda` tanpa mengubah pengalihan `/` → `/home`. Halaman ditaruh di route group `(blank-layout-pages)` yang sudah dipakai `/login` dan `/register` untuk halaman tanpa login; membuka route-nya di route guard adalah pekerjaan U-003.

## Anchors

- src/@layouts/BlankLayout.tsx:20 — layout kosong (tanpa navigasi dashboard) yang membungkus route group untuk halaman tanpa login; halaman baru cukup jadi `page.tsx` di dalam grup itu (layout grupnya tercatat di `existing_interfaces`)
- src/configs/themeConfig.ts:52 — pola modul konfigurasi statis bertipe di `src/configs/`

## Hard rules

- DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
  Source: binding.md §Suggested Unit Hard Rules (DO NOT modify package.json — C-MODE-01, C-AR-08); allowed_new_deps: []
- DO NOT modify next.config.ts
  Source: constraints.md OQ-AR-5 (Resolved v1.1 — pengalihan / → /home tidak diubah)
- file src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts MUST exist after bolt
  Source: constraints.md OQ-AR-4 (Resolved v1.1)
- MUST read the organization name, tagline, and services from src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts instead of hard-coding them in the page (constitution C-001)
  Source: constitution.md C-001
- MUST keep the Beranda layout usable at 375px wide and on desktop without horizontal scrolling (PRD §Halaman Beranda, C-CN-07)
  Source: binding.md C-CN-07 (constraints.md:18)

## Anti-patterns

- Jangan menaruh Beranda di `/` atau mengubah pengalihan `/` → `/home` (OQ-AR-5, next.config.ts:8).
- Jangan menambah CMS, multi-bahasa, atau autentikasi untuk konten ini (constitution D-001).

## Implementation steps

Pertama buat `src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts` sebagai modul bertipe (misalnya tipe `CompanyProfileConfig`) yang memuat `organizationName`, `tagline`, tepat tiga `services` (masing-masing `title` + `description`), `about.paragraphs` (dua sampai tiga paragraf untuk Tentang Kami), dan `team` (daftar `name` + `role`, tanpa foto) — semua isinya placeholder yang jelas terbaca sebagai contoh supaya tim bisa menggantinya sendiri, dan buat tipe `services` sebagai tuple tiga elemen agar jumlahnya dijaga oleh TypeScript. Lalu buat `src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/beranda/page.tsx` yang membaca konfigurasi itu dan merender judul organisasi sebagai heading utama, tagline, tiga kartu layanan, serta tombol berlabel Kontak yang menaut ke `/kontak` lewat `next/link`; susun dengan komponen MUI responsif (misalnya `Container` + `Grid`/`Stack`) supaya kartu menumpuk di 375px dan berjajar di desktop. Terakhir tulis `page.test.tsx` dengan `renderWithProviders` dari `src/test/utils.tsx`, memakai nama `it(...)` persis seperti di `acceptance_test`, termasuk satu test yang me-`vi.mock` modul konfigurasi dengan nilai lain untuk membuktikan halaman tidak menulis teks secara hard-code.

## Acceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria are the frontmatter `acceptance_test:` entries (authoritative).
- TBD: OQ-CN-3 — apakah syarat responsif juga berlaku untuk halaman lain belum diputuskan; di unit ini hanya Beranda yang wajib responsif.

## Out of scope

- Halaman Tentang Kami (U-002).
- Membuka `/beranda` di route guard `src/proxy.ts` (U-003).
- Form dan Halaman Kontak (U-004, U-005).

# Unit U-002 — Buat Halaman Tentang Kami

## Goal

Membuat Halaman Tentang Kami di `/tentang-kami` yang menampilkan profil singkat, daftar tim (nama + peran, tanpa foto), dan tautan kembali ke Beranda.

## Context (read first)

PRD §Halaman Tentang Kami meminta dua–tiga paragraf profil statis, daftar tim dari konfigurasi tanpa foto, dan tautan kembali ke Beranda; binding C-AR-02 mencatatnya sebagai pekerjaan baru. Kontennya dibaca dari `src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts` yang dibuat U-001 (OQ-AR-4), dan URL-nya `/tentang-kami` (OQ-AR-5), di route group `(blank-layout-pages)` yang sama dengan Beranda.

## Anchors

- src/@layouts/BlankLayout.tsx:20 — layout kosong (tanpa navigasi dashboard) yang membungkus route group halaman ini (layout grupnya tercatat di `existing_interfaces`)

## Hard rules

- DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
  Source: binding.md §Suggested Unit Hard Rules (DO NOT modify package.json — C-MODE-01, C-AR-08); allowed_new_deps: []
- DO NOT modify src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts
  Source: U-001 target_files (file owned by U-001); constraints.md OQ-AR-4 (Resolved v1.1)
- MUST read the profile paragraphs and the team list from src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts instead of hard-coding them in the page (constitution C-001)
  Source: constitution.md C-001

## Anti-patterns

- Jangan menampilkan foto anggota tim, termasuk avatar placeholder (constitution D-002, PRD §Halaman Tentang Kami).

## Implementation steps

Buat `src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/tentang-kami/page.tsx` yang mengimpor konfigurasi dari U-001 lalu merender heading halaman, setiap paragraf di `about.paragraphs` sebagai paragraf terpisah, dan daftar tim yang menampilkan nama serta peran tiap anggota sebagai teks saja, ditambah tautan kembali ke `/beranda` lewat `next/link`. Pakai komponen MUI yang sama gayanya dengan Beranda supaya kedua halaman terasa satu situs. Tulis `page.test.tsx` dengan `renderWithProviders` dari `src/test/utils.tsx` memakai nama `it(...)` persis seperti di `acceptance_test`, termasuk satu test yang me-`vi.mock` modul konfigurasi dengan nilai lain untuk membuktikan halaman tidak menulis teks secara hard-code, dan satu test yang memastikan tidak ada elemen `img` untuk anggota tim.

## Acceptance criteria

Acceptance criteria are the frontmatter `acceptance_test:` entries (authoritative).

## Out of scope

- Mengubah isi atau bentuk file konfigurasi (milik U-001).
- Membuka `/tentang-kami` di route guard `src/proxy.ts` (U-003).

5	import { authOptions } from './libs/auth'
6	
7	export async function proxy(request: Request) {
8	  const session = await getServerSession(authOptions)
9	  const { pathname } = new URL(request.url)
10	
11	  const publicRoutes = ['/login', '/register']
12	  const isPublicRoute = publicRoutes.includes(pathname)
13	
14	  if (session?.error === 'RefreshTokenError') {
15	    // Clear the session cookie and redirect — no signOut() needed here
16	    const response = NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))
17	
18	    response.cookies.delete('next-auth.session-token')
19	    response.cookies.delete('__Secure-next-auth.session-token') // for HTTPS
20	
21	    return response
22	  }
23	
24	  if (session?.accessToken && isPublicRoute) {
25	    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
26	  }
27	
28	  if (!session?.accessToken && !isPublicRoute) {
29	    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))
30	  }
31	
32	  return NextResponse.next()
33	}

1	# execute-bolts — Hard Rule pre/post-flight scan
2	
3	The anti-hallucination gate. Each unit's `## Hard rules` are validated against real codebase state **before** the bolt (pre-flight snapshot) and **after** the bolt (post-flight scan); any post-flight violation **HALTS the run**. Commit topology (detect-after — one truth, per SKILL.md): the `bolt-implementer` commits after its tests pass, so the post-flight scan runs against an already-committed bolt; a violation gates every further `execute-bolts` (B1) and the remediation is fix-forward or revert of the flagged commit — never a claim that the code is uncommitted. The skill body owns the gate's existence + trigger; this file owns the grammar, snapshot formats, and per-rule mechanics.
4	
5	## Contents
6	- Pre-flight: grammar detection
7	- Pre-flight: v2 (ast-grep) snapshot
8	- Pre-flight: v1 (legacy 5-grammar) snapshot
9	- `preflight.json` format
10	- Halt YAMLs (`hard_rule_unparseable`, `hard_rule_unanchored`)
11	- Post-flight: per-rule re-validation
12	- Framework-pack rule provenance
13	- Per-sibling cross-cutting registration scan
14	- Parent-thread post-flight re-scan
15	- Violation handling + `hard_rule_violated` halt YAML
16	- verify-unit special path
17	
18	## Pre-flight: grammar detection
19	
20	The entire pre-flight (grammar detection → per-rule validation → snapshot capture) is **executed by `scripts/run-preflight-scan.sh --cwd=<root> --units=U-001,U-002,…`** — the deterministic writer, called ONCE per batch with every target unit (`--unit=U-XXX` remains valid for a single unit). The controller runs the script and maps its exit code to the halt taxonomy; it never computes shas or emits the JSON itself (the artifact is hook-guarded — see §`preflight.json` format). Batch semantics: a FATAL code (3/4/5/6/8) stops the batch at the offending unit (named on stderr, unprocessed remainder listed); **exit 2 is a PRE-LOOP abort** (unresolvable unit id / usage / not a git repo) — nothing was processed, no baseline written for any unit, no remainder listing; exit 7 is per-unit and non-fatal — the batch continues and the final exit is 7 iff ≥1 unit was refused (each named on stderr):
21	
22	| Exit | Meaning → controller action |
23	|---|---|
24	| 0 | snapshot written / existing baseline kept (immutable) / no Hard rules — proceed |
25	| 2 | usage error (unit not found / not a git repo) — fix the invocation |
26	| 3 | halt `hard_rule_unparseable` (offending line / ast-grep stderr named verbatim) |
27	| 4 | halt `hard_rule_mixed_grammar` (`--grammar=v1\|v2` is the escape hatch) |
28	| 5 | halt `hard_rule_unanchored` (SIGNATURE_RULE symbol not in tracked source) |
29	| 6 | halt `dep_missing` (v2 grammar, ast-grep absent) |
30	| 7 | post-hoc refusal — bolt commits already exist and no baseline is on disk; NON-FATAL: proceed, post-flight falls back to commit evidence, log in the bolt-report |
31	| 8 | dirty-protected-path refusal — a rule target path (a `DO_NOT_MODIFY` path, or the file declaring a `SIGNATURE_RULE` symbol) differs from HEAD at baseline time; no artifact written. FATAL for this run (treat like a `hard_rule_violated`-style STOP, never proceed): commit or restore the protected file, then re-run — a dirty protected path at baseline time is indistinguishable from tampering |
32	
33	What the script executes, for each unit with a non-empty `## Hard rules` body section:
34	
35	- YAML code blocks under `## Hard rules` → **v2 grammar** (ast-grep YAML; the grammar spec is the v2 Hard-rule-grammar ref listed in SKILL.md).
36	- Bulleted line items (`- DO NOT modify ...`) → **v1 grammar** (the 5-type legacy set).
37	- Mixed (both forms in one unit) → halt `hard_rule_mixed_grammar` (user migrates via `migrate-rules`).
38	- Override via the script flag `--grammar=v1|v2` (the controller forwards the user-level `--hard-rule-grammar=v1|v2` value as `--grammar=<v>` on the script invocation — the script itself accepts only `--grammar`).
39	
40	**For v2 grammar:** probe `command -v ast-grep`. Absent → halt `dep_missing` (install guidance is in the v2 Hard-rule-grammar ref listed in SKILL.md). Validate each YAML block via parse-via-scan (`ast-grep test --validate` does NOT exist in the CLI — the snippet is in `hard-rule-grammar-v2.md` §Pre-flight, the single owner of the parse-check mechanics). Unparseable → halt `hard_rule_unparseable`.
41	
42	**For v1 grammar (legacy path preserved):** parse each rule line against the 5-grammar set per `generate-units/references/unit-schema.md` §Hard rule grammar (plus the directive tier — see §Directive rules below, which is ACCEPTED, not unparseable). NEVER silently skip a line that matches neither — unparseable → halt `hard_rule_unparseable`:
43	
44	- `DO NOT modify <path>`
45	- `DO NOT add new <manifest> dependencies`
46	- `<path-glob> MUST follow <case-style> naming`
47	- `function <name> MUST preserve signature: <type-sig>`
48	- `file <path> MUST exist after bolt`
49	
50	**Directive rules (third category — honest tier).** A generic `- MUST/MUST NOT/DO NOT/NEVER/ALWAYS …` prose line is ACCEPTED by the unit-stage validator (counted `hard_rules_directive_prose`) but is not machine-checkable by construction. At post-flight, `run-postflight-scan.sh` records such a rule as `type: directive` with verdict `directive_unverified`, or `attested` when the run passes `--attest-directives="<who/why>"` after controller/panel review. **Since 7.10.0 (spec 2026-08-30 §2.2, F-01a) directives are ADVISORY: neither verdict forms the artifact `status` or the B1 gate** — the verdict is formed by machine rules only, and the artifact carries a `directives: {total, attested, unverified}` summary. Measured basis: 256 of 278 field postflight rules were directives, every one "attested" by one free-text paragraph per unit, none could ever fail, and making them advisory lost zero detections. The panel is the reviewer of prose rules; B1 is the verifier of mechanical ones. **`--attest-directives` is blanket per run**: the one reason attests EVERY directive line in the unit (there is no per-rule attestation) — review ALL of them before attesting. Modal synonyms of the mechanical productions (`MUST NOT modify src/x.php`, `NEVER add new package.json dependencies`) classify as MECHANICAL, never directive — they cannot be attested past — **when the object is path-shaped** (contains `.` or `/`); a prose object (`MUST NOT modify existing API contracts`) stays a directive, because a mechanical check against a non-path would pass vacuously. A fabricated `pass` verdict on a directive line does not exist in the sanctioned writer's vocabulary.
51	
52	## Pre-flight: v2 (ast-grep) snapshot
53	
54	For each rule, snapshot AST state via `ast-grep scan --rule <yaml> --json` (zero matches expected pre-bolt for "forbidden" rules). Entries are recorded as `{type: v2_ast_grep, rule: <id>, matched_files: [{path, sha256}]}` in the same top-level `rules[]` array of `preflight.json` — an AUDIT record of the pre-bolt state, nothing more: post-flight re-runs the scan; it does NOT sha-compare (a v2 rule is a pattern scan, not a lock — the bolt may legitimately edit matched files to fix a pre-existing violation).
55	
56	## Pre-flight: v1 (legacy 5-grammar) snapshot
57	
58	- `DO_NOT_MODIFY <path>` → record `sha256(file content)` if the file exists; record "absent" otherwise.
59	- `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS <manifest>` → record the manifest's dependency-section content.
60	- `NAMING_RULE <path-glob> <case-style>` → no pre-snapshot (post-flight checks new files only).
61	- `SIGNATURE_RULE function <name>` → the script extracts the current declaration via the shared `find_decl_line` (the SAME extractor post-flight uses) and records the pre-`{` prefix as `signature_at_preflight`; symbol not found in tracked source → exit 5 → halt `hard_rule_unanchored`.
62	- `FILE_PRESENCE_RULE file <path>` → no pre-snapshot.
63	
64	## `preflight.json` format
65	
66	`run-preflight-scan.sh` persists the snapshot as `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/preflight.json` for post-flight comparison:
67	
68	```json
69	{
70	  "unit_id": "U-001",
71	  "snapshot_at": "2026-05-20T10:00:00Z",
72	  "head_sha": "<HEAD sha at capture>",
73	  "written_by": "run-preflight-scan.sh",
74	  "grammar": "v1",
75	  "rules": [
76	    {"type": "DO_NOT_MODIFY", "path": "src/Models/User.php", "sha256": "abc123..."},
77	    {"type": "DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS", "manifest": "package.json", "deps_section": "..."},
78	    {"type": "SIGNATURE_RULE", "function": "authenticateUser", "signature_at_preflight": "(email: string, password: string) => Promise<User>"}
79	  ]
80	}
81	```
82	
83	The `snapshot_at` / `head_sha` / `written_by` / `grammar` top-level keys are provenance stamps added by the script; the `rules[]` entry shapes are UNCHANGED (the post-flight engine reads only `rules[]`, so the stamps are ignored by every consumer). The artifact is **hook-guarded like `postflight.json`** — Write/Edit denied plus the Bash tamper verbs — because the engine gives a present sha/signature snapshot precedence over commit evidence: a hand-written baseline with a wrong sha256 is a forged BASELINE that makes a `DO_NOT_MODIFY`/`SIGNATURE` violation undetectable. Lifecycle rules:
84	
85	1. **Re-capture is allowed only while the unit has no bolt commits** — a re-run overwrites the snapshot (fresh `snapshot_at`).
86	2. **Once bolt commits exist the baseline is immutable** — an existing artifact is kept byte-identical; an absent one is refused with exit 7 (anti-laundering; post-flight then uses git commit evidence instead).
87	3. **A baseline is minted only from a tree whose protected paths match HEAD** — before minting, the writer compares every rule target path (`DO_NOT_MODIFY` paths AND the file declaring each `SIGNATURE_RULE` symbol) against HEAD; any difference is refused with exit 8 and NO artifact is written (tamper-BEFORE-mint would bake the tampered sha into the baseline, and the engine gives a present snapshot precedence over commit evidence). Remedy: commit or restore the protected file, then re-run — a dirty protected path at baseline time is indistinguishable from tampering. Unrelated dirty files never block; a legitimate clean-tree pre-flight is unaffected (HEAD == disk).
88	
89	## Halt YAMLs
90	
91	```yaml
92	blocker:
93	  type: hard_rule_unparseable
94	  emitted_at: <ISO8601>
95	  emitted_by: execute-bolts
96	  details:
97	    unit_id: U-XXX
98	    offending_line: "<verbatim>"
99	    expected_grammar: [DO_NOT_MODIFY, DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS, NAMING_RULE, SIGNATURE_RULE, FILE_PRESENCE_RULE]
100	  next_action: "Fix the unit's ## Hard rules section per generate-units/references/unit-schema.md §Hard rule grammar."
101	```
102	
103	```yaml
104	blocker:
105	  type: hard_rule_unanchored
106	  emitted_at: <ISO8601>
107	  emitted_by: execute-bolts
108	  details:
109	    unit_id: U-XXX
110	    rule: "function <name> MUST preserve signature: ..."
111	    reason: "Referenced function not found in tracked source (shared find_decl_line extractor); cannot snapshot or validate"
112	  next_action: "Verify the function name is correct OR remove this rule if the function doesn't exist yet."
113	```
114	
115	## Post-flight: per-rule re-validation
116	
117	After the implementer reports DONE (its commit already landed), run the post-flight scan via `scripts/run-postflight-scan.sh --cwd=<root> --unit=U-XXX` — the deterministic writer (the postflight.json artifact is hook-guarded; direct writes are denied). This is the safety net.
118	
119	**v2 grammar (ast-grep):**
120	
121	```bash
122	# Per rule: run ast-grep scan; any match against "forbidden" patterns = VIOLATED
123	ast-grep scan --rule <rule-yaml-tempfile> --json <repo-root>
124	```
125	
126	Parse the JSON output. Match found → VIOLATED with `file:line` + matched text as evidence. Zero matches → PASSED. (No sha256-vs-snapshot compare — lock semantics stay v1 `DO_NOT_MODIFY`; see the grammar ref's mapping table.)
127	
128	**v1 grammar (legacy, preserved):**
129	
130	| Rule type | Post-flight check |
131	|---|---|
132	| `DO_NOT_MODIFY <path>` | Compute current `sha256(file)`. Compare to preflight snapshot. Differs OR file appeared → VIOLATED. |
133	| `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS <manifest>` | Read current manifest deps section. Diff against preflight snapshot. ANY new entry → VIOLATED. |
134	| `NAMING_RULE <path-glob> <case-style>` | Enumerate new files matching `path-glob`. Apply case-style regex. Mismatch → VIOLATED. |
135	| `SIGNATURE_RULE function <name>` | Re-extract current signature from codebase. Compare to preflight. Differs → VIOLATED. |
136	| `FILE_PRESENCE_RULE file <path>` | Probe `<path>` exists. Absent → VIOLATED. |
137	
138	Post-flight results are written to `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/postflight.json` (per-rule pass/fail + evidence):
139	
140	```json
141	{
142	  "unit_id": "U-001",
143	  "scanned_at": "2026-05-20T10:05:00Z",
144	  "status": "pass",
145	  "rules": [
146	    {"type": "DO_NOT_MODIFY", "path": "src/Models/User.php", "verdict": "pass", "evidence": "sha256 unchanged"},
147	    {"type": "SIGNATURE_RULE", "function": "authenticateUser", "verdict": "pass", "evidence": "signature preserved"}
148	  ]
149	}
150	```
151	
152	**Mandatory evidence (B1 — enforced, not prose).** For a committed `create`/`extend` bolt whose unit has a **non-empty `## Hard rules`** section, this `postflight.json` MUST exist with `status: pass` and every MACHINE rule `rules[].verdict: pass` (directive-typed rules are advisory since 7.10.0 — recorded, never gating) — and it is written by `run-postflight-scan.sh` and hook-guarded against direct writes plus the common programmatic write paths (and, since v4.62.0, **RECOMPUTED at the gate**: `validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --postflight-scan --recompute` re-executes each committed Hard-rule bolt's mechanical rules from git/fs ground truth via the shared `scripts/_lib/postflight_rules.py` engine and OVERWRITES the artifact before the state is read — a forged/stale/absent artifact is regenerated; directives keep their prior human attestation via carry-forward). The Stop hook AND the execute-bolts gate re-run `validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --postflight-scan`; the PreToolUse aggregator **blocks the next `execute-bolts`** with **`postflight_evidence_missing`** when a Hard-rule bolt committed with no passing `postflight.json` — the post-flight scan can no longer be silently skipped or satisfied by a naive hand-written artifact. The validator reads the unit's content at the bolt commit (`git show`), so a retroactive unit edit cannot erase the obligation. Verify units skip post-flight (no changes to validate), so they are exempt. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-batch-suite-gate-and-bypass-guard.md §B1`.
153	
154	> `--force-skip-postflight` skips the ast-grep step for ONE run only and is logged per the SKILL.md anti-bypass policy (handoff `notes.postflight_skipped: true` + `_summary.md`). It does NOT downgrade the rail; a follow-up re-run without the flag is required before drift-detect / merge.
155	
156	## Framework-pack rule provenance
157	
158	Framework-pack rules (pulled into a unit's Hard Rules by `generate-units` Step 12.4.5) are validated identically to other Hard Rules — Step 12.4.5 emits them **in an executable production** (packs ship `rule_type` inventories, not ready-made ast-grep blocks; the translation happens at emission time per the pack→bolt table in `bind-codebase/references/hard-rules-and-packs.md §2.9a` — v1 production, verbatim v2 YAML when the pack carries a real `rule:` body, or the honest `directive`/Anti-pattern tier). The violation surface includes a `framework_pack_source` field in the halt YAML so the user knows WHICH framework rule fired.
159	
160	## Per-sibling cross-cutting registration scan (defense-in-depth)
161	
162	When a unit fans out into N structurally-analogous sibling models (a module's golden exemplar plus siblings), a cross-cutting concern proven on the exemplar (e.g. registering the `BranchScoped` global scope) must be verified in EACH sibling's generated source — not once. The classic execution-fidelity miss: every sibling SPEC named the `BranchScoped` trait, but the bolt forgot the `addGlobalScope(new BranchScoped)` registration in several generated models — a silent cross-branch authorization leak that no unit-spec or Hard-Rule check catches (the spec was correct; the runtime call was dropped).
163	
164	This is ENFORCED by `scripts/the --cross-cutting mode of validate-sibling-consistency.sh`, which reads the active framework pack's `## Cross-cutting concerns` (each concern's `registration_signature` + `registration_target_glob`) and scans every generated source file that references the concern mechanism AND carries the `applies_when` column, flagging any that lack the registration call. It runs PostToolUse on model/source writes (→ `.cross-cutting-state.json`); PreToolUse Branch 11 blocks the NEXT `execute-bolts` on FAIL (honest detect-and-block-next — a hook cannot un-write a file a bolt just wrote mid-turn). This prose is defense-in-depth; the validator is the gate. Tech-agnostic: never assume a stack's registration idiom — it comes from the pack, so add a stack = add a pack.
165	
166	## Parent-thread post-flight re-scan
167	
168	The project-wide quality validators that scan GENERATED SOURCE/VIEWS — `the --cross-cutting mode of validate-sibling-consistency.sh`, `validate-ui-quality.sh`, and (for vault edits) `validate-vault-oqs.sh` — fire via PostToolUse on the writer's Write/Edit. # execute-bolts — Hard Rule pre/post-flight scan

The anti-hallucination gate. Each unit's `## Hard rules` are validated against real codebase state **before** the bolt (pre-flight snapshot) and **after** the bolt (post-flight scan); any post-flight violation **HALTS the run**. Commit topology (detect-after — one truth, per SKILL.md): the `bolt-implementer` commits after its tests pass, so the post-flight scan runs against an already-committed bolt; a violation gates every further `execute-bolts` (B1) and the remediation is fix-forward or revert of the flagged commit — never a claim that the code is uncommitted. The skill body owns the gate's existence + trigger; this file owns the grammar, snapshot formats, and per-rule mechanics.

## Contents
- Pre-flight: grammar detection
- Pre-flight: v2 (ast-grep) snapshot
- Pre-flight: v1 (legacy 5-grammar) snapshot
- `preflight.json` format
- Halt YAMLs (`hard_rule_unparseable`, `hard_rule_unanchored`)
- Post-flight: per-rule re-validation
- Framework-pack rule provenance
- Per-sibling cross-cutting registration scan
- Parent-thread post-flight re-scan
- Violation handling + `hard_rule_violated` halt YAML
- verify-unit special path

## Pre-flight: grammar detection

The entire pre-flight (grammar detection → per-rule validation → snapshot capture) is **executed by `scripts/run-preflight-scan.sh --cwd=<root> --units=U-001,U-002,…`** — the deterministic writer, called ONCE per batch with every target unit (`--unit=U-XXX` remains valid for a single unit). The controller runs the script and maps its exit code to the halt taxonomy; it never computes shas or emits the JSON itself (the artifact is hook-guarded — see §`preflight.json` format). Batch semantics: a FATAL code (3/4/5/6/8) stops the batch at the offending unit (named on stderr, unprocessed remainder listed); **exit 2 is a PRE-LOOP abort** (unresolvable unit id / usage / not a git repo) — nothing was processed, no baseline written for any unit, no remainder listing; exit 7 is per-unit and non-fatal — the batch continues and the final exit is 7 iff ≥1 unit was refused (each named on stderr):

| Exit | Meaning → controller action |
|---|---|
| 0 | snapshot written / existing baseline kept (immutable) / no Hard rules — proceed |
| 2 | usage error (unit not found / not a git repo) — fix the invocation |
| 3 | halt `hard_rule_unparseable` (offending line / ast-grep stderr named verbatim) |
| 4 | halt `hard_rule_mixed_grammar` (`--grammar=v1\|v2` is the escape hatch) |
| 5 | halt `hard_rule_unanchored` (SIGNATURE_RULE symbol not in tracked source) |
| 6 | halt `dep_missing` (v2 grammar, ast-grep absent) |
| 7 | post-hoc refusal — bolt commits already exist and no baseline is on disk; NON-FATAL: proceed, post-flight falls back to commit evidence, log in the bolt-report |
| 8 | dirty-protected-path refusal — a rule target path (a `DO_NOT_MODIFY` path, or the file declaring a `SIGNATURE_RULE` symbol) differs from HEAD at baseline time; no artifact written. FATAL for this run (treat like a `hard_rule_violated`-style STOP, never proceed): commit or restore the protected file, then re-run — a dirty protected path at baseline time is indistinguishable from tampering |

What the script executes, for each unit with a non-empty `## Hard rules` body section:

- YAML code blocks under `## Hard rules` → **v2 grammar** (ast-grep YAML; the grammar spec is the v2 Hard-rule-grammar ref listed in SKILL.md).
- Bulleted line items (`- DO NOT modify ...`) → **v1 grammar** (the 5-type legacy set).
- Mixed (both forms in one unit) → halt `hard_rule_mixed_grammar` (user migrates via `migrate-rules`).
- Override via the script flag `--grammar=v1|v2` (the controller forwards the user-level `--hard-rule-grammar=v1|v2` value as `--grammar=<v>` on the script invocation — the script itself accepts only `--grammar`).

**For v2 grammar:** probe `command -v ast-grep`. Absent → halt `dep_missing` (install guidance is in the v2 Hard-rule-grammar ref listed in SKILL.md). Validate each YAML block via parse-via-scan (`ast-grep test --validate` does NOT exist in the CLI — the snippet is in `hard-rule-grammar-v2.md` §Pre-flight, the single owner of the parse-check mechanics). Unparseable → halt `hard_rule_unparseable`.

**For v1 grammar (legacy path preserved):** parse each rule line against the 5-grammar set per `generate-units/references/unit-schema.md` §Hard rule grammar (plus the directive tier — see §Directive rules below, which is ACCEPTED, not unparseable). NEVER silently skip a line that matches neither — unparseable → halt `hard_rule_unparseable`:

- `DO NOT modify <path>`
- `DO NOT add new <manifest> dependencies`
- `<path-glob> MUST follow <case-style> naming`
- `function <name> MUST preserve signature: <type-sig>`
- `file <path> MUST exist after bolt`

**Directive rules (third category — honest tier).** A generic `- MUST/MUST NOT/DO NOT/NEVER/ALWAYS …` prose line is ACCEPTED by the unit-stage validator (counted `hard_rules_directive_prose`) but is not machine-checkable by construction. At post-flight, `run-postflight-scan.sh` records such a rule as `type: directive` with verdict `directive_unverified`, or `attested` when the run passes `--attest-directives="<who/why>"` after controller/panel review. **Since 7.10.0 (spec 2026-08-30 §2.2, F-01a) directives are ADVISORY: neither verdict forms the artifact `status` or the B1 gate** — the verdict is formed by machine rules only, and the artifact carries a `directives: {total, attested, unverified}` summary. Measured basis: 256 of 278 field postflight rules were directives, every one "attested" by one free-text paragraph per unit, none could ever fail, and making them advisory lost zero detections. The panel is the reviewer of prose rules; B1 is the verifier of mechanical ones. **`--attest-directives` is blanket per run**: the one reason attests EVERY directive line in the unit (there is no per-rule attestation) — review ALL of them before attesting. Modal synonyms of the mechanical productions (`MUST NOT modify src/x.php`, `NEVER add new package.json dependencies`) classify as MECHANICAL, never directive — they cannot be attested past — **when the object is path-shaped** (contains `.` or `/`); a prose object (`MUST NOT modify existing API contracts`) stays a directive, because a mechanical check against a non-path would pass vacuously. A fabricated `pass` verdict on a directive line does not exist in the sanctioned writer's vocabulary.

## Pre-flight: v2 (ast-grep) snapshot

For each rule, snapshot AST state via `ast-grep scan --rule <yaml> --json` (zero matches expected pre-bolt for "forbidden" rules). Entries are recorded as `{type: v2_ast_grep, rule: <id>, matched_files: [{path, sha256}]}` in the same top-level `rules[]` array of `preflight.json` — an AUDIT record of the pre-bolt state, nothing more: post-flight re-runs the scan; it does NOT sha-compare (a v2 rule is a pattern scan, not a lock — the bolt may legitimately edit matched files to fix a pre-existing violation).

## Pre-flight: v1 (legacy 5-grammar) snapshot

- `DO_NOT_MODIFY <path>` → record `sha256(file content)` if the file exists; record "absent" otherwise.
- `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS <manifest>` → record the manifest's dependency-section content.
- `NAMING_RULE <path-glob> <case-style>` → no pre-snapshot (post-flight checks new files only).
- `SIGNATURE_RULE function <name>` → the script extracts the current declaration via the shared `find_decl_line` (the SAME extractor post-flight uses) and records the pre-`{` prefix as `signature_at_preflight`; symbol not found in tracked source → exit 5 → halt `hard_rule_unanchored`.
- `FILE_PRESENCE_RULE file <path>` → no pre-snapshot.

## `preflight.json` format

`run-preflight-scan.sh` persists the snapshot as `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/preflight.json` for post-flight comparison:

```json
{
  "unit_id": "U-001",
  "snapshot_at": "2026-05-20T10:00:00Z",
  "head_sha": "<HEAD sha at capture>",
  "written_by": "run-preflight-scan.sh",
  "grammar": "v1",
  "rules": [
    {"type": "DO_NOT_MODIFY", "path": "src/Models/User.php", "sha256": "abc123..."},
    {"type": "DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS", "manifest": "package.json", "deps_section": "..."},
    {"type": "SIGNATURE_RULE", "function": "authenticateUser", "signature_at_preflight": "(email: string, password: string) => Promise<User>"}
  ]
}
```

The `snapshot_at` / `head_sha` / `written_by` / `grammar` top-level keys are provenance stamps added by the script; the `rules[]` entry shapes are UNCHANGED (the post-flight engine reads only `rules[]`, so the stamps are ignored by every consumer). The artifact is **hook-guarded like `postflight.json`** — Write/Edit denied plus the Bash tamper verbs — because the engine gives a present sha/signature snapshot precedence over commit evidence: a hand-written baseline with a wrong sha256 is a forged BASELINE that makes a `DO_NOT_MODIFY`/`SIGNATURE` violation undetectable. Lifecycle rules:

1. **Re-capture is allowed only while the unit has no bolt commits** — a re-run overwrites the snapshot (fresh `snapshot_at`).
2. **Once bolt commits exist the baseline is immutable** — an existing artifact is kept byte-identical; an absent one is refused with exit 7 (anti-laundering; post-flight then uses git commit evidence instead).
3. **A baseline is minted only from a tree whose protected paths match HEAD** — before minting, the writer compares every rule target path (`DO_NOT_MODIFY` paths AND the file declaring each `SIGNATURE_RULE` symbol) against HEAD; any difference is refused with exit 8 and NO artifact is written (tamper-BEFORE-mint would bake the tampered sha into the baseline, and the engine gives a present snapshot precedence over commit evidence). Remedy: commit or restore the protected file, then re-run — a dirty protected path at baseline time is indistinguishable from tampering. Unrelated dirty files never block; a legitimate clean-tree pre-flight is unaffected (HEAD == disk).

## Halt YAMLs

```yaml
blocker:
  type: hard_rule_unparseable
  emitted_at: <ISO8601>
  emitted_by: execute-bolts
  details:
    unit_id: U-XXX
    offending_line: "<verbatim>"
    expected_grammar: [DO_NOT_MODIFY, DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS, NAMING_RULE, SIGNATURE_RULE, FILE_PRESENCE_RULE]
  next_action: "Fix the unit's ## Hard rules section per generate-units/references/unit-schema.md §Hard rule grammar."
```

```yaml
blocker:
  type: hard_rule_unanchored
  emitted_at: <ISO8601>
  emitted_by: execute-bolts
  details:
    unit_id: U-XXX
    rule: "function <name> MUST preserve signature: ..."
    reason: "Referenced function not found in tracked source (shared find_decl_line extractor); cannot snapshot or validate"
  next_action: "Verify the function name is correct OR remove this rule if the function doesn't exist yet."
```

## Post-flight: per-rule re-validation

After the implementer reports DONE (its commit already landed), run the post-flight scan via `scripts/run-postflight-scan.sh --cwd=<root> --unit=U-XXX` — the deterministic writer (the postflight.json artifact is hook-guarded; direct writes are denied). This is the safety net.

**v2 grammar (ast-grep):**

```bash
# Per rule: run ast-grep scan; any match against "forbidden" patterns = VIOLATED
ast-grep scan --rule <rule-yaml-tempfile> --json <repo-root>
```

Parse the JSON output. Match found → VIOLATED with `file:line` + matched text as evidence. Zero matches → PASSED. (No sha256-vs-snapshot compare — lock semantics stay v1 `DO_NOT_MODIFY`; see the grammar ref's mapping table.)

**v1 grammar (legacy, preserved):**

| Rule type | Post-flight check |
|---|---|
| `DO_NOT_MODIFY <path>` | Compute current `sha256(file)`. Compare to preflight snapshot. Differs OR file appeared → VIOLATED. |
| `DO_NOT_ADD_DEPS <manifest>` | Read current manifest deps section. Diff against preflight snapshot. ANY new entry → VIOLATED. |
| `NAMING_RULE <path-glob> <case-style>` | Enumerate new files matching `path-glob`. Apply case-style regex. Mismatch → VIOLATED. |
| `SIGNATURE_RULE function <name>` | Re-extract current signature from codebase. Compare to preflight. Differs → VIOLATED. |
| `FILE_PRESENCE_RULE file <path>` | Probe `<path>` exists. Absent → VIOLATED. |

Post-flight results are written to `<vault>/bolts/U-XXX/postflight.json` (per-rule pass/fail + evidence):

```json
{
  "unit_id": "U-001",
  "scanned_at": "2026-05-20T10:05:00Z",
  "status": "pass",
  "rules": [
    {"type": "DO_NOT_MODIFY", "path": "src/Models/User.php", "verdict": "pass", "evidence": "sha256 unchanged"},
    {"type": "SIGNATURE_RULE", "function": "authenticateUser", "verdict": "pass", "evidence": "signature preserved"}
  ]
}
```

**Mandatory evidence (B1 — enforced, not prose).** For a committed `create`/`extend` bolt whose unit has a **non-empty `## Hard rules`** section, this `postflight.json` MUST exist with `status: pass` and every MACHINE rule `rules[].verdict: pass` (directive-typed rules are advisory since 7.10.0 — recorded, never gating) — and it is written by `run-postflight-scan.sh` and hook-guarded against direct writes plus the common programmatic write paths (and, since v4.62.0, **RECOMPUTED at the gate**: `validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --postflight-scan --recompute` re-executes each committed Hard-rule bolt's mechanical rules from git/fs ground truth via the shared `scripts/_lib/postflight_rules.py` engine and OVERWRITES the artifact before the state is read — a forged/stale/absent artifact is regenerated; directives keep their prior human attestation via carry-forward). The Stop hook AND the execute-bolts gate re-run `validate-bolt-artifacts.sh --postflight-scan`; the PreToolUse aggregator **blocks the next `execute-bolts`** with **`postflight_evidence_missing`** when a Hard-rule bolt committed with no passing `postflight.json` — the post-flight scan can no longer be silently skipped or satisfied by a naive hand-written artifact. The validator reads the unit's content at the bolt commit (`git show`), so a retroactive unit edit cannot erase the obligation. Verify units skip post-flight (no changes to validate), so they are exempt. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-batch-suite-gate-and-bypass-guard.md §B1`.

> `--force-skip-postflight` skips the ast-grep step for ONE run only and is logged per the SKILL.md anti-bypass policy (handoff `notes.postflight_skipped: true` + `_summary.md`). It does NOT downgrade the rail; a follow-up re-run without the flag is required before drift-detect / merge.

## Framework-pack rule provenance

Framework-pack rules (pulled into a unit's Hard Rules by `generate-units` Step 12.4.5) are validated identically to other Hard Rules — Step 12.4.5 emits them **in an executable production** (packs ship `rule_type` inventories, not ready-made ast-grep blocks; the translation happens at emission time per the pack→bolt table in `bind-codebase/references/hard-rules-and-packs.md §2.9a` — v1 production, verbatim v2 YAML when the pack carries a real `rule:` body, or the honest `directive`/Anti-pattern tier). The violation surface includes a `framework_pack_source` field in the halt YAML so the user knows WHICH framework rule fired.

## Per-sibling cross-cutting registration scan (defense-in-depth)

When a unit fans out into N structurally-analogous sibling models (a module's golden exemplar plus siblings), a cross-cutting concern proven on the exemplar (e.g. registering the `BranchScoped` global scope) must be verified in EACH sibling's generated source — not once. The classic execution-fidelity miss: every sibling SPEC named the `BranchScoped` trait, but the bolt forgot the `addGlobalScope(new BranchScoped)` registration in several generated models — a silent cross-branch authorization leak that no unit-spec or Hard-Rule check catches (the spec was correct; the runtime call was dropped).

This is ENFORCED by `scripts/the --cross-cutting mode of validate-sibling-consistency.sh`, which reads the active framework pack's `## Cross-cutting concerns` (each concern's `registration_signature` + `registration_target_glob`) and scans every generated source file that references the concern mechanism AND carries the `applies_when` column, flagging any that lack the registration call. It runs PostToolUse on model/source writes (→ `.cross-cutting-state.json`); PreToolUse Branch 11 blocks the NEXT `execute-bolts` on FAIL (honest detect-and-block-next — a hook cannot un-write a file a bolt just wrote mid-turn). This prose is defense-in-depth; the validator is the gate. Tech-agnostic: never assume a stack's registration idiom — it comes from the pack, so add a stack = add a pack.

## Parent-thread post-flight re-scan

The project-wide quality validators that scan GENERATED SOURCE/VIEWS — `the --cross-cutting mode of validate-sibling-consistency.sh`, `validate-ui-quality.sh`, and (for vault edits) `validate-vault-oqs.sh` — fire via PostToolUse on the writer's Write/Edit. PostToolUse DOES fire on bolt-agent writes (it fires inside subagents — AUDIT L1), so the state is not "invisible"; but under `--parallel` / `--per-squad` the project-wide state can lag concurrent write ordering (each validator is a full-glob current-truth re-scan, and the async hook may not have settled). To make the gate state deterministic: after each bolt batch completes, the **main-thread controller** explicitly bash-invokes those validators against `$PROJECT_ROOT` **with `--quiet`, branching on the exit code** — read the specific `.mega-sdd/.<validator>-state.json` ONLY on non-zero (M-05: the PreToolUse gate reads state files, never stdout; an unquieted PASS printed full state JSON incl. the ~350-char canned next_action per validator) — so the gate reflects current truth regardless of write ordering. This is **defense-in-depth** on top of the detect-and-block-next contract — not a load-bearing compensation for an invisible write.

## Violation handling + `hard_rule_violated` halt YAML

- **ANY rule violated → HALT the run (detect-after).** The violating code is already committed (the implementer commits before the scan). The user reviews + fixes forward or `git revert`s the bolt commit; the B1 gate blocks every further `execute-bolts` until a passing `postflight.json` is recorded by `run-postflight-scan.sh`.
- Emit the `hard_rule_violated` blocker YAML with `violated_rule` + evidence.
- `bolt-report.md` MUST be written with `status: halted_postflight` and list the violations.

```yaml
blocker:
  type: hard_rule_violated
  emitted_at: <ISO8601>
  emitted_by: execute-bolts
  details:
    unit_id: U-XXX
    committed: true          # detect-after — the bolt commit already landed
    commit: <bolt commit sha>
    violations:
      - rule: "DO NOT modify src/Models/User.php"
        evidence: "sha256 mismatch — preflight: abc123..., postflight: def456..."
      - rule: "function authenticateUser MUST preserve signature: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<User>"
        evidence: "Signature changed; postflight: (email: string, password: string, twoFactor?: string) => Promise<User>"
  next_action: "The violation is in commit <sha>: fix the code forward (or git revert the bolt commit), then re-run run-postflight-scan.sh; execute-bolts stays gated until a passing postflight.json is recorded. If the RULE is wrong, edit the unit's Hard rules AND COMMIT the edit as `fix(U-XXX): correct hard rule` — the gate recomputes against the unit text AT the bolt commit, so an uncommitted working-tree edit is silently overridden at the next gate (the writer's pass would be provisional)."
```

## verify-unit special path

`task_type: verify` units run a simplified flow (no code write):

1. Pre-flight: validate the unit's `target_files` is empty / all `operation: none` (else halt `verify_unit_writable` — verify units are read-only and must never be written).
2. Skip `executing-plans` (no code to write).
3. Run acceptance tests.
4. Skip the post-flight Hard-rule scan (no changes to validate).
5. Commit only `bolt-report.md` (no source changes); OR skip the commit entirely on `--no-empty-commits`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# merge-panel-findings.sh — the SOLE writer of <vault>/bolts/U-XXX/findings.json
# (spec 2026-08-29 Fase 1).
#
# Why this exists. The severity->status mapping in review-panel.md §Attempt
# rounds was PROSE, applied by whatever model was driving the controller. Field
# measurement (HOST-AS400 U-001, panel complete, spec_verdict pass): 2 critical
# + 7 important + 4 minor, and ALL THIRTEEN were stamped `status: open`. The
# contract says Critical and the findings behind a spec-fail enter as `open`;
# Important/Minor enter as `advisory` — recorded, surfaced, NEVER gating. So 11
# of 13 findings (85%) held the fix round hostage: the implementer's fix scope
# and the resolution-verifier's workload both scaled by 6.5x over a naming nit.
# Prose that says "never gating" enforces nothing (gates > rules > hooks).
#
# What it does, deterministically:
#   1. Parse each lens's FINDINGS: block (rows `severity | file:line | title | detail`).
#   2. Evidence-or-drop — a row with no resolvable file:line is DISCARDED and counted.
#   3. Dedup — same (file, +/-3 lines, same title stem) across lenses -> ONE entry at
#      MAX severity, `lenses[]` records every reporter.
#   4. Consensus — reported by >=2 lenses -> confidence: high.
#   5. Status mapping — critical UNION spec-fail-linked -> open; important/minor ->
#      advisory. This is the whole point; it is not a judgment call.
#   6. Stable IDs across rounds — an existing finding keeps its id and its
#      resolution history; a re-reported issue never gets a duplicate new id.
#
# Verifier rounds (--verifier=<file>) consume RESOLUTIONS: + NEW-FINDINGS: and
# apply the same mapping to the new rows; `resolved` REQUIRES new-head evidence
# (a resolution row with no file:line stays open — evidence-gated resolution).
#
# Usage:
#   merge-panel-findings.sh --vault=<dir> --unit=U-XXX --head=<sha> [--round=N]
#       [--spec-verdict=pass|fail] --lens=<name>:<file> [--lens=... ...]
#   merge-panel-findings.sh --vault=<dir> --unit=U-XXX --head=<sha> --round=N
#       --verifier=<file>
#
# Exit: 0 = ledger written (stdout = one-line JSON summary incl. gate verdict)
#       2 = usage error. Never exits non-zero on findings — the GATE reads
#           `open_count` from the summary/ledger; this script records, it does
#           not decide to halt.
set -u

VAULT=""; UNIT=""; HEAD_SHA=""; ROUND=1; SPEC_VERDICT=""; VERIFIER=""
LENSES=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  --vault=*) VAULT="${1#*=}"; shift;;

21	## File location standards
22	
23	| Artifact | Path |
24	|---|---|
25	| App root layout | `app/layout.tsx` |
26	| Pages (App Router) | `app/**/page.tsx` |
27	| Layouts (App Router) | `app/**/layout.tsx` |
28	| Route Handlers (App Router) | `app/**/route.ts` |
29	| Loading UI | `app/**/loading.tsx` |
30	| Error UI | `app/**/error.tsx` |
31	| Not-found UI | `app/**/not-found.tsx` |
32	| Pages (Pages Router) | `pages/**/*.tsx` (legacy alternative to App Router) |
33	| API Routes (Pages Router) | `pages/api/**/*.ts` (legacy alternative to `app/**/route.ts`) |
34	| Shared components | `components/` |
35	| Utility / helper modules | `lib/` |
36	| Static assets | `public/` |
37	| Global middleware | `middleware.ts` (project root) |
38	| TypeScript config | `tsconfig.json` |
39	| Next.js config | `next.config.ts` / `next.config.mjs` |
40	| Environment variables | `.env.local`, `.env.production`, `.env` |
41	| Tests | `__tests__/` or co-located `*.test.tsx` / `*.spec.tsx` |
42	| End-to-end tests | `e2e/` or `tests/e2e/` (Playwright) |
43	
44	## Naming standards
45	
46	| Concept | Convention | Example |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| Page file (App Router) | reserved name `page.tsx` | `app/dashboard/page.tsx` |
49	| Layout file (App Router) | reserved name `layout.tsx` | `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx` |
50	| Route Handler file | reserved name `route.ts` | `app/api/users/route.ts` |
51	| Special files | lowercase reserved names | `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`, `template.tsx` |
52	| Route segment (folder) | kebab-case | `app/user-profile/page.tsx` |
53	| Route group (non-routing folder) | `(group-name)` — lowercase kebab in parens | `app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` |
54	| Dynamic segment | `[param]` or `[...slug]` (catch-all) | `app/posts/[id]/page.tsx` |
55	| Private folder (excluded from routing) | `_folder` prefix | `app/_components/` |
56	| Component filename | PascalCase `.tsx` | `components/UserCard.tsx` |
57	| Component name | PascalCase | `UserCard`, `NavBar` |
58	| Server Component | PascalCase, no directive (default) | `app/dashboard/page.tsx` |
59	| Client Component | PascalCase + `"use client"` directive at top | `components/Counter.tsx` |
60	| Hook | camelCase, `use` prefix | `useAuthSession`, `useCart` |
61	| Utility / helper | camelCase or kebab-case file | `lib/formatDate.ts`, `lib/auth-helpers.ts` |
62	| Type / interface | PascalCase | `UserProfile`, `ApiResponse<T>` |
63	| Environment variable | `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix for client-exposed; all-caps snake | `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, `DATABASE_URL` |
64	
65	## Idioms (preferred patterns)
66	
67	- **Server Components by default** — every component in `app/` is a React Server Component unless `"use client"` is declared; fetch data directly in RSC with `async/await` without client-side state
68	- **`"use client"` directive at the top of interactive components** — only mark components that need browser APIs, event listeners, or React state/effects as Client Components
69	- **`"use server"` for Server Actions** — co-locate or extract data-mutation logic in `async` functions marked `"use server"`; call them from forms or Client Components for server-side mutations without a separate API layer
70	- **Data fetching in Server Components** — prefer `fetch()` with Next.js extended caching options (`cache: 'force-cache'`, `next: { revalidate: N }`) over client-side `useEffect` fetching
71	- **Route Handlers for API endpoints** — define `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH` named exports in `app/**/route.ts` for explicit HTTP API routes
72	- **Metadata API for SEO** — export a `metadata` object or `generateMetadata()` function from `page.tsx` / `layout.tsx` rather than using `<Head>` tags
73	- **Nested layouts for shared UI** — use nested `layout.tsx` files to share persistent UI across route segments without re-rendering
74	- **`next/image` for images** — always use the `<Image>` component from `next/image` for automatic optimization, lazy loading, and responsive sizes
75	- **`next/link` for navigation** — use `<Link>` from `next/link` for client-side navigation; avoid raw `<a>` for internal routes
76	- **`next/font` for fonts** — use the built-in font optimization module instead of manual `@font-face` or CDN font links
77	- **Parallel and Intercepting Routes** — use `@slot` and `(.)route` conventions for advanced routing patterns like modals and parallel dashboards
78	- **Server Actions for form mutations** — prefer `action={serverAction}` on `<form>` elements over manual POST fetch calls
79	- **Middleware for edge-level logic** — use `middleware.ts` for auth redirects, locale detection, header injection; keep it lightweight (runs at the Edge)
80

- **Nested layouts for shared UI** — use nested `layout.tsx` files to share persistent UI across route segments without re-rendering
- **`next/image` for images** — always use the `<Image>` component from `next/image` for automatic optimization, lazy loading, and responsive sizes
- **`next/link` for navigation** — use `<Link>` from `next/link` for client-side navigation; avoid raw `<a>` for internal routes
- **`next/font` for fonts** — use the built-in font optimization module instead of manual `@font-face` or CDN font links
- **Parallel and Intercepting Routes** — use `@slot` and `(.)route` conventions for advanced routing patterns like modals and parallel dashboards
- **Server Actions for form mutations** — prefer `action={serverAction}` on `<form>` elements over manual POST fetch calls
- **Middleware for edge-level logic** — use `middleware.ts` for auth redirects, locale detection, header injection; keep it lightweight (runs at the Edge)

123	## Security idioms
124	
125	> Consumed by the review-panel `security-reviewer` lens (pack security slice) and by
126	> `bolt-implementer` via T2 framework-pack rules. Stack-correct, mechanism-named —
127	> the dangerous bypass is spelled out next to each idiom.
128	
129	- **Input validation** — `zod` parse at the server boundary: inside every Server Action (`formData` → schema) and Route Handler (`await request.json()` → schema); the bypass is trusting the payload shape because "the form only sends these fields" — client-side validation is not validation, both surfaces are directly callable.
130	- **SQL injection** — Prisma/Drizzle parameterize; `prisma.$queryRawUnsafe` or building SQL with string concatenation inside a tagged template reintroduces SQLi — use the tagged-template bindings (`sql\`… ${v}\``) or stay in the ORM query API.
131	- **XSS / output escaping** — React auto-escapes JSX output; `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is the named bypass, valid only for server-sanitized HTML. Also watch user-controlled `href` values rendering `javascript:` URLs.
132	- **CSRF** — Server Actions have built-in origin checking (POST-only + Origin/Host match); Route Handlers do NOT — a cookie-authenticated handler needs `SameSite` cookies plus an explicit origin check. The bypass is a state-changing Route Handler (or a mutating GET) that trusts cookies with no origin/token check.
133	- **AuthN/AuthZ enforcement point** — `middleware.ts` for coarse redirects, but real authorization is the session check inside each Route Handler, Server Action, and data-access function; the classic bypass is protecting only the page UI (or only middleware) while the API route and server action underneath stay open to direct requests.
134	- **Password hashing** — `bcrypt`/`argon2` in server-only code (Server Actions, Route Handlers, `lib/` server modules); never imported into a `"use client"` file.
135	- **Mass assignment** — the zod schema's parsed output is the field allowlist; the bypass is `Object.fromEntries(formData)` or a raw body passed straight into `prisma.user.update({ data })`, letting an extra `role` field escalate privileges.
136	- **Secrets / config** — anything prefixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_` is compiled into the client bundle; server secrets stay unprefixed and are read only in server code. The bypass is importing a server-env module from a `"use client"` component, or "temporarily" renaming a secret to `NEXT_PUBLIC_` to make a build pass (pack hard rule).
137	- **File uploads** — handle uploads server-side only (Route Handler/Server Action) with size caps and a mimetype allowlist, stored outside `public/`; for `next/image` remote sources, constrain `images.remotePatterns` in `next.config` so the optimizer is not an open image proxy.

 *   C-DM-05 "**`created_at`**: terisi saat pesan valid disimpan (PRD §Alur F-U-001 — Definition of Done).";
 *   C-FL-02 "`name` wajib, maksimal 100 karakter"; C-FL-03 "`email` wajib, format email valid";

 * Anchors consulted: src/app/api/v1/users/route.ts:4; src/libs/api/route-handler.ts:43;
 *   src/features/users/schemas/user.schema.ts:3; src/test/handlers.ts:49
 * Hard Rules active:
 *   - DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
 *   - DO NOT modify src/libs/api/route-handler.ts
 *   - file src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.ts MUST exist after bolt
 *   - MUST validate name, email and message on the server with the shared schema before anything is forwarded (constitution B-001)
 *   - MUST forward valid messages to the upstream API through proxyPost from src/libs/api/route-handler.ts (constitution C-002)
 *   - NEVER persist the message in this app or add a database client (OQ-AR-1)
 */
import { z } from 'zod'

/**
 * Contact-form message, shared by the server route and the browser form so both
 * enforce the same rules. Every field is trimmed before its length checks, so a
 * whitespace-only value counts as empty. The limits match the upstream storage
 * columns (name 100, email 255) and the PRD cap on message length (2000).
 *
 * Error texts are short placeholders kept in this one file so they are easy to
 * replace once final copy is decided.
 */
export const contactMessageSchema = z.object({
  name: z
    .string({ error: 'Nama wajib diisi' })
    .trim()
    .min(1, 'Nama wajib diisi')
    .max(100, 'Nama maksimal 100 karakter'),

  // Trim first, then check the format: `z.email().trim()` would check the
  // format before trimming and reject an address with surrounding spaces.
  email: z
    .string({ error: 'Email wajib diisi' })
    .trim()
    .min(1, 'Email wajib diisi')
    .max(255, 'Email maksimal 255 karakter')
    .pipe(z.email('Format email tidak valid')),

  message: z
    .string({ error: 'Pesan wajib diisi' })
    .trim()
    .min(1, 'Pesan wajib diisi')
    .max(2000, 'Pesan maksimal 2000 karakter')
})

export type ContactMessageValues = z.infer<typeof contactMessageSchema>

export const contactMessageDefaults: ContactMessageValues = {
  name: '',
  email: '',
  message: ''
}

119	  rule_type: LOCATION_RULE
120	  rationale: Next.js requires a root layout that wraps all routes and supplies the html/body shell
121	```
122	
123	## Security idioms
124	
125	> Consumed by the review-panel `security-reviewer` lens (pack security slice) and by
126	> `bolt-implementer` via T2 framework-pack rules. Stack-correct, mechanism-named —
127	> the dangerous bypass is spelled out next to each idiom.
128	
129	- **Input validation** — `zod` parse at the server boundary: inside every Server Action (`formData` → schema) and Route Handler (`await request.json()` → schema); the bypass is trusting the payload shape because "the form only sends these fields" — client-side validation is not validation, both surfaces are directly callable.
130	- **SQL injection** — Prisma/Drizzle parameterize; `prisma.$queryRawUnsafe` or building SQL with string concatenation inside a tagged template reintroduces SQLi — use the tagged-template bindings (`sql\`… ${v}\``) or stay in the ORM query API.
131	- **XSS / output escaping** — React auto-escapes JSX output; `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is the named bypass, valid only for server-sanitized HTML. Also watch user-controlled `href` values rendering `javascript:` URLs.
132	- **CSRF** — Server Actions have built-in origin checking (POST-only + Origin/Host match); Route Handlers do NOT — a cookie-authenticated handler needs `SameSite` cookies plus an explicit origin check. The bypass is a state-changing Route Handler (or a mutating GET) that trusts cookies with no origin/token check.
133	- **AuthN/AuthZ enforcement point** — `middleware.ts` for coarse redirects, but real authorization is the session check inside each Route Handler, Server Action, and data-access function; the classic bypass is protecting only the page UI (or only middleware) while the API route and server action underneath stay open to direct requests.
134	- **Password hashing** — `bcrypt`/`argon2` in server-only code (Server Actions, Route Handlers, `lib/` server modules); never imported into a `"use client"` file.
135	- **Mass assignment** — the zod schema's parsed output is the field allowlist; the bypass is `Object.fromEntries(formData)` or a raw body passed straight into `prisma.user.update({ data })`, letting an extra `role` field escalate privileges.
136	- **Secrets / config** — anything prefixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_` is compiled into the client bundle; server secrets stay unprefixed and are read only in server code. The bypass is importing a server-env module from a `"use client"` component, or "temporarily" renaming a secret to `NEXT_PUBLIC_` to make a build pass (pack hard rule).
137	- **File uploads** — handle uploads server-side only (Route Handler/Server Action) with size caps and a mimetype allowlist, stored outside `public/`; for `next/image` remote sources, constrain `images.remotePatterns` in `next.config` so the optimizer is not an open image proxy.
138	
139	## Testing conventions
140	
141	- **Unit / integration runner**: Jest (common default) or Vitest — configured via `jest.config.ts` / `vitest.config.ts`
142	- **React component testing**: React Testing Library (`@testing-library/react`) + `@testing-library/jest-dom` for DOM matchers
143	- **End-to-end testing**: Playwright (`@playwright/test`) — config in `playwright.config.ts`; tests in `e2e/` or `tests/e2e/`
144	- **Test file location**: co-located `ComponentName.test.tsx` next to the component, or aggregated under `__tests__/`
145	- **Test naming**: describe/it blocks — `describe('UserCard', () => { it('renders user name', ...) })`
146	- **Server Component testing**: render with React's `renderToString` or wrap with a test `Suspense` boundary; mock `next/navigation` and `next/headers` modules
147	- **Mocking next modules**: use `jest.mock('next/navigation')` / `jest.mock('next/headers')` to isolate components from Next.js routing/cookie APIs in unit tests
148	- **MSW (Mock Service Worker)**: common choice for intercepting `fetch` calls in integration tests without a real server
149	- **Coverage**: `jest --coverage` or `vitest run --coverage`; `lcov` format for CI integration

# Bolt report — U-004 "Buat skema validasi dan route kirim pesan kontak"

**Status:** DONE
**Commit:** 9270bf5aa5197537c1e4529bb7db7c8f7a9b9b84 (on detached HEAD, parent fe0843b)

## What was implemented

- `src/features/contact/schemas/contact.schema.ts` — `contactMessageSchema` (name: trim, required, max 100; email: trim, required, max 255, then piped into `z.email`; message: trim, required, max 2000), `ContactMessageValues` (`z.infer`), `contactMessageDefaults`. Missing fields get the same "wajib diisi" message as empty ones.
- `src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.ts` — `POST`: `req.json()` in try/catch → 400 `{success:false, code:'BAD_REQUEST', message, data:null}`; `safeParse` failure → 422 `{success:false, code:'VALIDATION_ERROR', message, data:{fieldErrors}}` without calling upstream; valid → new `NextRequest` carrying only the parsed `{name, email, message}` handed to the module-scope `proxyPost('/v1/contact-messages')` handler, whose response is returned unchanged.
- `src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.test.ts` — 11 acceptance cases with `it(...)` names verbatim from `acceptance_test`, plus one extra case ("trims surrounding whitespace before forwarding"). `next-auth` mocked so `getServerSession` returns null; upstream captured via `server.use(http.post('http://localhost:3000/v1/contact-messages', …))`.

## Tests

- TDD red run: `Failed to resolve import "./route" ... Does the file exist?` (right reason — route absent).
- First green attempt: 6/12 failed with `ReferenceError: NextRequest is not defined` (type-only import used as a value) → fixed to a value import.
- Final: `pnpm vitest run src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.test.ts --reporter=verbose` → 12 passed (12).
- Full suite `pnpm test:run` → 7 files, 50 tests passed. `eslint` clean on all three files; `tsc --noEmit -p .` clean.
- Manual acceptance (real upstream, `contact_messages` row with `created_at`) — not executable here; needs a real upstream providing `POST /v1/contact-messages`.

## Hard rules honored

- DO NOT add new package.json dependencies — package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml unchanged (zod 4.3.6, msw already installed).
- DO NOT modify src/libs/api/route-handler.ts — unchanged (`git diff HEAD` empty).
- file src/app/api/v1/contact-messages/route.ts MUST exist after bolt — created.
- MUST validate name, email and message on the server with the shared schema before anything is forwarded — `contactMessageSchema.safeParse` runs before any forward; tests assert zero upstream calls on failure.
- MUST forward valid messages to the upstream API through proxyPost — the only upstream path is `proxyPost('/v1/contact-messages')`.
- NEVER persist the message in this app or add a database client — nothing stored; no DB client.

## reuse_decisions

- candidate: `proxyPost` (src/libs/api/route-handler.ts) — decision: reused (unchanged; wrapped by a rebuilt request so only validated fields reach it).
- candidate: `apiServer` (src/libs/api/server.ts) — decision: reused (indirectly, via proxyPost; not called by hand).
- candidate: `ApiResponse` (src/types/common.ts) — decision: reused (`satisfies ApiResponse<…>` on the 400/422 envelopes).
- candidate: `server` MSW instance (src/test/handlers.ts) — decision: reused (`server.use`), harness files not modified.
- candidate: `z.flattenError` (zod 4.3.6) — decision: reused for `fieldErrors`.
- candidate: existing feature schemas (users/roles/permissions/profile) — decision: not_applicable (no contact fields; pattern followed only).
- reuse-index.yaml is absent at `.mega-sdd/codebase/reuse-index.yaml` (recorded in dispatch omissions); scanned `.mega-sdd/codebase/symbol-index.json` instead — no contact/validation helper exists.

## Notes / concerns

- Provenance marker version `v7.34.0` was sourced from the dispatch's `## Contracts (agent-carried)` line, because the `Provenance values` block carries no version key. All other trailer values come verbatim from that block.
- A JSON body that is not an object (e.g. `null`, array) yields 422 with `fieldErrors: {}` (zod reports it as a form-level error). Status and top-level message still correct; not a crash.
- Upstream failures: a non-OK upstream status and a 200 `success:false` envelope both come back as HTTP 400 (proxyPost's fixed mapping). OQ-FL-2 minimum (non-2xx) satisfied; finer status mapping would require changing route-handler.ts, which is forbidden.

  confidence: 0.9
  certain_decisions:
    - "Trim before length checks on every field; email uses trim→min→max→pipe(z.email) because z.email().trim() checks format before trimming (verified: padded address rejected)."
    - "Forward a rebuilt NextRequest with only parsed {name,email,message} to a module-scope proxyPost handler; never the raw body."
    - "422 VALIDATION_ERROR with data.fieldErrors and 400 BAD_REQUEST with data:null, per the implementation steps; upstream never called in either case."
    - "Test names copied verbatim from acceptance_test; email length test proves 255 accepted / 256 rejected so the max rule, not format, is what fails."

      rationale: "OQ-FL-1 leaves final copy open; the consumer is the public Halaman Kontak whose labels (Nama/Email/Pesan) and success text ('Pesan terkirim') are Indonesian, and U-005 may not modify this schema."

**Status: DONE.** The contact-message schema and the `POST /api/v1/contact-messages` route are built and committed as `9270bf5` (`feat(U-004): Buat skema validasi dan route kirim pesan kontak`). All 11 acceptance tests pass, and so do the full suite, lint, the type-check and a production build.

## What was built
- **Schema** (`contactMessageSchema`, `ContactMessageValues`, `contactMessageDefaults`), in the same layout as the users schema:
  - All three fields are trimmed first, so a field of only spaces counts as empty.
  - `name` is required, at most 100 characters.
  - `email` is required, at most 255 characters, and must be a valid format. The format check has to come after the trim: I found that zod's `z.email().trim()` checks the format first and rejects an address with surrounding spaces.
  - `message` is required, at most 2000 characters.
  - A missing field gets the same "wajib diisi" message as an empty one.
- **Route `POST`** (the route does not store anything):
  - A body that isn't valid JSON gets HTTP 400, code `BAD_REQUEST`.
  - Invalid input gets HTTP 422, code `VALIDATION_ERROR`, with errors per field and a readable top-level message. The upstream API is not called.
  - A valid message is sent to upstream `POST /v1/contact-messages` through `proxyPost`, carrying only the checked, trimmed `{name, email, message}` (never the raw browser body). Upstream's response is returned unchanged.

## Tests
- I wrote the test first; it failed because `./route` didn't exist yet.
- The first full run failed 6 of 12 because the route imported `NextRequest` as a type only. After fixing that, all 12 pass (the 11 acceptance cases named exactly as in the unit, plus one extra check that values are trimmed before forwarding).
- Full suite: 7 files, 50 tests pass. Lint and `tsc --noEmit` are clean, and `pnpm build` succeeds and lists the new route.
- The manual acceptance check (a real upstream storing a row with `created_at`) could not be run here.

## Hard rules (all six honored)
- No new dependencies; `package.json` and the lockfile are unchanged.
- `src/libs/api/route-handler.ts` is unchanged.
- `route.ts` exists.
- The shared schema validates on the server before anything is forwarded; the tests confirm upstream is not called when validation fails.
- `proxyPost` is the only way the route calls upstream.
- Nothing is stored in this app and no database client was added.

## reuse_decisions
- `proxyPost` — reused, unchanged.
- `apiServer` — reused indirectly through `proxyPost`.
- `ApiResponse` — reused to type the 400 and 422 responses.
- MSW `server` from `src/test/handlers.ts` — reused via `server.use`; the harness files were not edited.
- `z.flattenError` (zod 4.3.6) — reused for the per-field errors.
- Existing feature schemas — not_applicable; followed as a pattern only.
- `reuse-index.yaml` does not exist, so I scanned `.mega-sdd/codebase/symbol-index.json` instead. No contact or validation helper exists; nothing was rewritten from scratch.

## Decisions and open points
- **Error text is in Indonesian** ("Nama wajib diisi", "Format email tidak valid", and so on). The wording is still an open question in the PRD, and the page showing these errors is labelled in Indonesian, while the existing admin schemas use English. U-005 is not allowed to edit this schema, so if English is wanted the strings must be changed in the schema and route files; the tests check that errors appear, not their wording.
- **Upstream failures always come back as HTTP 400,** whether upstream sends an error status or a 200 with `success: false`. That mapping is fixed inside `proxyPost`, which I may not modify. It meets the "non-2xx" minimum the unit asks for.
- **A JSON body that isn't an object** (e.g. `null`) gets a 422 with an empty field-error list and the normal top-level message. It does not crash.
- **Provenance trailers** are in all three files. The dispatch's values block has no version, so I took `v7.34.0` from its Contracts line. The ids in the trailers, such as `(constitution B-001)` and `(OQ-AR-1)`, are part of the hard-rule text copied as instructed, not citations I added; no ordinary code comment cites a vault id.
- The bolt report (self-report and rollback hints) is written but not committed, which matches sibling U-001's commit.

44	# Unit U-001 — Buat konten statis profil dan Halaman Beranda
45	
46	## Goal
47	
48	Membuat file konfigurasi konten profil (placeholder) dan Halaman Beranda di `/beranda` yang menampilkan judul organisasi, tagline, tiga layanan utama, dan tombol menuju Kontak.
49	
50	## Context (read first)
51	
52	PRD §Halaman Beranda meminta judul organisasi, tagline satu kalimat, ringkasan tiga layanan (judul + satu paragraf, statis dari file konfigurasi), dan tombol ke Kontak, responsif di 375px dan desktop; binding C-AR-01/C-AR-04 mencatat semuanya sebagai pekerjaan baru. OQ-AR-4 memutuskan konten tinggal di satu modul TypeScript bertipe `src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts`, dan OQ-AR-5 memutuskan URL `/beranda` tanpa mengubah pengalihan `/` → `/home`. Halaman ditaruh di route group `(blank-layout-pages)` yang sudah dipakai `/login` dan `/register` untuk halaman tanpa login; membuka route-nya di route guard adalah pekerjaan U-003.
53	
54	## Anchors
55	
56	- src/components/Providers.tsx:18 — provider (NextAuth, TanStack Query, tema — tanpa SnackbarProvider) yang dipasang layout route group halaman tanpa login bersama BlankLayout; halaman baru cukup jadi `page.tsx` di dalam grup itu (layout grupnya tercatat di `existing_interfaces`)
57	- src/configs/themeConfig.ts:52 — pola modul konfigurasi statis bertipe di `src/configs/`
58	
59	## Hard rules
60	
61	- DO NOT add new package.json dependencies
62	  Source: binding.md §Suggested Unit Hard Rules (DO NOT modify package.json — C-MODE-01, C-AR-08); allowed_new_deps: []
63	- DO NOT modify next.config.ts
64	  Source: constraints.md OQ-AR-5 (Resolved v1.1 — pengalihan / → /home tidak diubah)
65	- file src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts MUST exist after bolt
66	  Source: constraints.md OQ-AR-4 (Resolved v1.1)
67	- MUST read the organization name, tagline, and services from src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts instead of hard-coding them in the page (constitution C-001)
68	  Source: constitution.md C-001
69	- MUST keep the Beranda layout usable at 375px wide and on desktop without horizontal scrolling (PRD §Halaman Beranda, C-CN-07)
70	  Source: binding.md C-CN-07 (constraints.md:18)
71	
72	## Anti-patterns
73	
74	- Jangan menaruh Beranda di `/` atau mengubah pengalihan `/` → `/home` (OQ-AR-5, next.config.ts:8).
75	- Jangan menambah CMS, multi-bahasa, atau autentikasi untuk konten ini (constitution D-001).
76	
77	## Implementation steps
78	
79	Pertama buat `src/configs/companyProfileConfig.ts` sebagai modul bertipe (misalnya tipe `CompanyProfileConfig`) yang memuat `organizationName`, `tagline`, tepat tiga `services` (masing-masing `title` + `description`), `about.paragraphs` (dua sampai tiga paragraf untuk Tentang Kami), dan `team` (daftar `name` + `role`, tanpa foto) — semua isinya placeholder yang jelas terbaca sebagai contoh supaya tim bisa menggantinya sendiri, dan buat tipe `services` sebagai tuple tiga elemen agar jumlahnya dijaga oleh TypeScript. Lalu buat `src/app/(blank-layout-pages)/beranda/page.tsx` yang membaca konfigurasi itu dan merender judul organisasi sebagai heading utama, tagline, tiga kartu layanan, serta tombol berlabel Kontak yang menaut ke `/kontak` lewat `next/link`; susun dengan komponen MUI responsif (misalnya `Container` + `Grid`/`Stack`) supaya kartu menumpuk di 375px dan berjajar di desktop. Terakhir tulis `page.test.tsx` dengan `renderWithProviders` dari `src/test/utils.tsx`, memakai nama `it(...)` persis seperti di `acceptance_test`, termasuk satu test yang me-`vi.mock` modul konfigurasi dengan nilai lain untuk membuktikan halaman tidak menulis teks secara hard-code.
80	
81	## Acceptance criteria
82	
83	Acceptance criteria are the frontmatter `acceptance_test:` entries (authoritative).
84	
85	- TBD: OQ-CN-3 — apakah syarat responsif juga berlaku untuk halaman lain belum diputuskan; di unit ini hanya Beranda yang wajib responsif.
86	
87	## Out of scope
88	
89	- Halaman Tentang Kami (U-002).
90	- Membuka `/beranda` di route guard `src/proxy.ts` (U-003).
91	- Form dan Halaman Kontak (U-004, U-005).
